title: Measuring in vitro ATPase Activity with High Sensitivity Using Radiolabeled ATP

Recipes Note: Since low quantities of free phosphate are quantified, a phosphate contamination of the used reagents and material should be minimized. A control sample only containing buffer should be used for detection of the background signal and data correction. Assay buffer (100 mL) 20 mM HEPES (4.766 g), 150 mM NaCl (8.766 g), 20% (w/v) glycerol (20 g), 0.05% (w/v) DDM (250 μL of 20% stock; see Recipe 2), pH 7.4. Weigh NaCl, glycerol, and HEPES and fill up to 90 mL with ddH 2 O. Adjust the pH with 1 M NaOH to 7.4. Add DDM and fill up to 100 mL with ddH 2 O. Note: For other ATPases, this buffer may be adapted. 20% (w/v) DDM stock (5 mL) Dissolve 1 g of DDM in 3 mL of ddH 2 O in a 15 mL polypropylene screw-cap tube and incubate with head-over-head rotation until completely dissolved. Let the foam set and fill up to a total of 5 mL with ddH 2 O. Store at 4 °C. 1 M HCl (100 mL) Dilute 8.3 mL of concentrated (37%) HCl to a total volume of 100 mL with ddH 2 O. Reagent A (15 mL) Dissolve 0.185 g of ammonium heptamolybdate tetrahydrate in a total volume of 15 mL in 1 M HCl. Note: Prepare fresh on the day of the experiment. Per sample, 1.5 mL of Reagent A is needed. We recommend preparing a sufficient volume for one extra sample. Reagent B (33.3 mL) Mix isobutanol, cyclohexane, acetone, and Reagent A in a glass flask in a ratio of 5:5:1:0.1 (v:v) by circular movements, resulting in 45% (v/v) isobutanol (15 mL), 45% (v/v) cyclohexane (15 mL), 9% (v/v) acetone (3 mL), and 0.1% Reagent A (0.3 mL) for 33.3 mL. Note: Substances used are volatile and toxic. Work under the fume hood. Prepare fresh on the day of the experiment. Per sample, 3 mL of Reagent B is needed. We recommend preparing a sufficient volume for one extra sample. 20 mM H 3 PO 4 (5 mL) Dilute 6.5 μL of 85% (w/w) orthophosphoric acid to a total of 5 mL in ddH 2 O. 100 mM ATP (10 mL) Dissolve 551 mg of ATP in a total volume of 8 mL in ddH 2 O. Adjust pH to 7.0 with 1 M KOH. Fill up to 10 mL with ddH 2 O. Freeze aliquots of e.g., 200 μL in 1.5 mL polypropylene reaction tubes at -20 °C. Avoid repeated freeze-thawing. 500 mM MgCl 2 (10 mL) Dissolve 1.017 g of MgCl 2 hexahydrate in a total volume of 10 mL in ddH 2 O. Store at RT. 700 mM orthovanadate (35 mL) Add 4.5 g of sodium orthovanadate to 30 mL of ddH 2 O in a glass beaker and stir until completely dissolved. Adjust the pH to 10 using 1 M NaOH or 1 M HCl. Note: Acidification leads to a color change to yellow. Boil the solution on a heating plate with continuous stirring until the solution loses its color. Let cool to room temperature and measure pH. Titrate again to pH 10 using 1 M NaOH or 1 M HCl and repeat boiling and titration until pH = 10 is stable at room temperature. Fill up with ddH 2 O to 35 mL. Store aliquots of e.g., 200 μL in 1.5 mL polypropylene reaction tubes at -20 °C. Directly before use, heat the solution for 15 min at 95 °C to break polymeric species ( Goodno, 1982 ) and place it on ice until use. Note: Orthovanadate is toxic. Work under the fume hood and wear protective gear.

steps.title: Gather materials and reagents
steps.instruction: Collect all listed consumables and chemicals with their catalog numbers: polypropylene tubes (1.5 mL, 2 mL, 15 mL; Sarstedt 72.690.001, 72.691, 62.554.502), 15 mL glass tubes with screwable lid (Oehmen 7920120, 6702588), filter tips (10 µL, 200 µL, 1 mL; Starlab S1120-3810, S1120-8810, S1126-7810), 5 mL pipette tips (Gilson F161571), 4 mL scintillation vials (PerkinElmer 1200-421), glass beakers (100 mL), glass flasks (500 mL), measuring flasks (100 mL), magnetic stir bars, safety goggles, gloves, DDM (Glycon D97002), HEPES (Roth 6763.3), NaCl (Fisher 10284640), glycerol (>99 %, VWR 24388.295), NaOH (Sigma‑Aldrich 30620), MgCl₂·6H₂O (Sigma‑Aldrich M2670), isobutanol (Alfa Aesar B23091), cyclohexane (VWR 23224.293), acetone (Sigma‑Aldrich 904082), non‑radioactive ATP (Sigma A3377), ammonium heptamolybdate tetrahydrate (Roth 3666.1), scintillation fluid (Roth 0016.3), HCl (VWR 20252.290), 85 % H₃PO₄ (VWR 20624.295), KOH (Fisher P564060), [γ‑³²P]‑ATP (PerkinElmer BLU502H, 3 000 Ci/mmol, 5 mCi/mL, 250 µCi, store at 4 °C), sodium orthovanadate (Sigma 450243). Also have the purified ATPase (Apt1p‑GFP/Cdc50p‑Flag) at 1.026 mg L⁻¹ in assay buffer (20 mM HEPES‑NaOH pH 7.5, 20 % glycerol, 150 mM NaCl, 0.04 % DDM) stored at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare assay buffer (100 mL)
steps.instruction: Weigh 4.766 g HEPES, 8.766 g NaCl, and 20 g glycerol. Add ddH₂O to 90 mL, adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 M NaOH, add 0.05 % (w/v) DDM (250 µL of 20 % DDM stock, see step 3), then bring volume to 100 mL with ddH₂O. Store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 20 % DDM stock (5 mL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g DDM in 3 mL ddH₂O in a 15 mL polypropylene screw‑cap tube, rotate until fully dissolved, let foam settle, then add ddH₂O to a final volume of 5 mL. Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M HCl solution
steps.instruction: Dilute 8.3 mL concentrated 37 % HCl with ddH₂O to a final volume of 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare Reagent A (15 mL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.185 g ammonium heptamolybdate tetrahydrate in 15 mL 1 M HCl. Prepare fresh on the day of the experiment; 1.5 mL per sample plus extra for one additional sample.

steps.title: Prepare Reagent B (33.3 mL)
steps.instruction: In a glass flask, mix isobutanol, cyclohexane, acetone, and Reagent A in a volume ratio of 5:5:1:0.1 (v/v) by circular movements to obtain 45 % (v/v) isobutanol (15 mL), 45 % cyclohexane (15 mL), 9 % acetone (3 mL), and 0.1 % Reagent A (0.3 mL) for a total of 33.3 mL. Prepare fresh on the day of the experiment; 3 mL per sample plus extra for one additional sample. Work under a fume hood.

steps.title: Prepare 20 mM H₃PO₄ (5 mL)
steps.instruction: Dilute 6.5 µL of 85 % (w/w) orthophosphoric acid to 5 mL with ddH₂O.

steps.title: Prepare 100 mM ATP stock (10 mL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 551 mg ATP in 8 mL ddH₂O, adjust pH to 7.0 with 1 M KOH, then bring volume to 10 mL with ddH₂O. Aliquot (e.g., 200 µL) into 1.5 mL polypropylene tubes and store at –20 °C; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Prepare 500 mM MgCl₂ stock (10 mL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.017 g MgCl₂·6H₂O in 10 mL ddH₂O. Store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 700 mM orthovanadate stock (35 mL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 4.5 g sodium orthovanadate in 30 mL ddH₂O, stir until fully dissolved, adjust pH to 10 with 1 M NaOH or 1 M HCl. Boil the solution with continuous stirring until the yellow color disappears, cool to room temperature, re‑adjust pH to 10, repeat boiling and titration until pH 10 is stable. Bring volume to 35 mL with ddH₂O, aliquot (≈200 µL) into 1.5 mL tubes, store at –20 °C. Directly before use, heat at 95 °C for 15 min to destroy polymers and keep on ice. Orthovanadate is toxic; handle in a fume hood with protective gear.

steps.title: Prepare 10× ATPase reaction mix
steps.instruction: Calculate the activity of the [γ‑³²P]‑ATP for the day using A(t)=A₀·e^(–λt) (λ derived from half‑life 14.29 days). Using the calibration date, determine the current specific activity. For each sample, the 10× mix contains 0.5 µL of 100 mM ATP (final 1 mM), 0.5 µL of 500 mM MgCl₂ (final 5 mM), 3.6 µL assay buffer, and 0.4 µL of [γ‑³²P]‑ATP at 0.4 µCi µL⁻¹ (total 2 µCi per 5 µL). Prepare the mix without the radiolabel first, then add the calculated volume of [γ‑³²P]‑ATP to reach 0.4 µCi µL⁻¹. Adjust the final volume to 5 µL per sample with assay buffer. Prepare an excess for calibration reference samples (three extra 5 µL mixes). From this point onward, handle all material as radioactive, using Perspex shielding, Geiger monitoring, and dosimeters as required.

steps.title: Thaw and aliquot purified ATPase
steps.instruction: Retrieve the purified Apt1p‑GFP/Cdc50p‑Flag protein (1.026 mg L⁻¹ in assay buffer, stored at –80 °C). Thaw slowly on ice. Aliquot small volumes to avoid multiple freeze‑thaws; keep on ice until use.

steps.title: Set up reaction samples and controls
steps.instruction: In 2 mL polypropylene reaction tubes on ice, prepare 45 µL final volume per sample using the assay buffer. Follow the pipetting scheme (Table 1): for each duplicate, add 39 µL protein solution (≈40–250 ng protein), 0 µL inhibitor (or 1 µL orthovanadate if testing inhibition), and 5 µL assay buffer. For buffer‑only blanks, add 45 µL assay buffer. Prepare calibration reference tubes with 0.2 µL of a 1:10 dilution of the 10× mix (i.e., 2 µL of 1:10 diluted mix). Store all tubes on ice.

steps.title: Incubate inhibitor samples (if used)
steps.instruction: If orthovanadate is used as inhibitor, add 1 µL (final 1 mM) to the appropriate protein tubes, then incubate 20 min at room temperature on ice to allow inhibition. Boiled orthovanadate (15 min at 95 °C) must be kept on ice until use.

steps.title: Add 10× mix to samples on ice
steps.instruction: Pipette 5 µL of the prepared 10× ATPase reaction mix (containing the calculated [γ‑³²P]‑ATP) into each 45 µL sample tube while keeping the tubes on ice.

steps.title: Start ATPase reaction (28 °C, 60 min)
steps.instruction: Transfer the tubes to a thermomixer set to 28 °C, gentle shaking not exceeding 700 rpm, and incubate for 60 min. This temperature may be optimized for other ATPases.

steps.title: Terminate reaction and add Reagent A
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on ice immediately after incubation and add 1.5 mL of Reagent A to each tube to stop the reaction and inactivate the ATPase.

steps.title: Transfer to glass tube with H₃PO₄
steps.instruction: Move each reaction mixture into a separate 15 mL glass tube containing 15 µL of 20 mM H₃PO₄ (carrier for inorganic phosphate).

steps.title: Add Reagent B, vortex, ice incubation
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL of Reagent B to each glass tube, fasten the lid, vortex for 30 s, then incubate on ice for 10 min to allow phase separation. Work under a fume hood because Reagent B is volatile.

steps.title: Prepare scintillation vials
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL of scintillation fluid to each 4 mL scintillation vial (PerkinElmer 1200‑421). Label the side of each vial (not the lid) because the MicroBeta2 measures through the lid.

steps.title: Transfer organic phase to scintillation fluid
steps.instruction: After phase separation, carefully pipette 500 µL of the yellow upper organic phase (containing the radioactive orthophosphate‑molybdate complex) into the scintillation fluid of the corresponding vial. Avoid pipetting up‑and‑down to prevent scintillation fluid from entering the tip.

steps.title: Prepare calibration reference samples
steps.instruction: Make a 1:10 dilution of the 10× ATPase reaction mix by mixing 2 µL of the mix with 18 µL H₂O. Add 2 µL of this dilution to the scintillation fluid in three separate vials to serve as calibration references. Perform each in triplicate.

steps.title: Perform scintillation counting (MicroBeta2)
steps.instruction: Tighten vial lids, place vials in the measuring cassette, invert several times to mix, and insert the cassette into the MicroBeta2 counter with the stop cassette below. In the MicroBeta2 Windows Workstation, create a protocol: set Label 1 to “32 P”, Label 2 to “None”, Plate/Filter to “4 mL plate 6 × 4”, Assay Type to “Normal”, counting time 1 min, Detector Normalization and Background correction to “None”, counting precision 0.2 2 σ%, cycling parameter 1 time per plate. Adjust the plate setup to read only the slots containing vials, then start the measurement. Export CPM values as .txt files.
